assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes; daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: ready.

## Reasoning

**Agent.** Muse's runtime executes shell tool calls autonomously and reports both a low-level 'effect' view (kind:"task"/tool_batch.effect.*) and a higher-level pairing directly under kind:"run": assistant_tool_calls_committed (opens, carrying tool_calls[].call_id/name) and tool_result_batch_committed (closes, carrying results[].tool_call_id) — muse-format-spec.md §4, cross-checked against real captures. Critically, format-spec §4 also documents the discriminator this scenario hinges on: a tool call's side_effect_intent.policy_decision is "allow:policy" for a policy-fast-tracked, read-only command (the exact observed example is `bash "ls -la"`, executed "with no wait") — that call never enters the kind:"approval" flow at all. A tool call that instead needs review goes through a SEPARATE, structurally distinct requested → automated_review_started → automated_review_completed → decision_applied record family before its tool_batch.effect.started fires (format-spec §4-5). So muse genuinely performs BOTH the auto-executed happy path and a review-gated path, and the transcript tells them apart.

**Daemon.** The now-built Go adapter (core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go) implements exactly this distinction: parseRunStarted (parser.go:308-315) sets EventType="user_message" on kind:"run" event.kind:"started" (ready→working); parseRunTerminal (parser.go:324-365) sets EventType="turn_done" on event.kind:"terminal" (working→ready), independent of the completed/cancelled/failed outcome. parseAssistantToolCallsCommitted (parser.go:445-) and parseToolResultBatchCommitted (parser.go:467-) populate ToolUses/ToolResultIDs paired by call_id — this is the ONLY tool-call source the parser wires (a deliberate choice documented at parser.go:57-74: the task/tool_batch.effect.* family carries the identical call_id but would be pure duplication). Waiting is sourced exclusively from kind:"approval" requested/decision_applied (parser.go:76-83, parseApprovalRequested/parseApprovalDecisionApplied at parser.go:550,563), which set PermissionRequestIDs/PermissionResolvedIDs — the transcript-tier TranscriptPermissionPending signal the daemon's state_classifier reads to enter `waiting`. A policy-fast-tracked call ("allow:policy") produces NO kind:"approval" record at all, so PermissionRequestIDs is never opened and `waiting` is structurally unreachable for that call — this is a real, code-grounded guarantee, not an inference. Unit coverage exists for both halves: TestParseLine_ToolCall_OpenAndClose_PairByCallID (parser_test.go:270) and TestParseLine_ApprovalRequested_OpensPermission / TestParseLine_ApprovalDecisionApplied_ClosesPermission (parser_test.go:323,335). `go test ./core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/... -race -count=1` passes (verified by exit code, this session).

**Driver.** replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh's DRIVE_ELICITS (line 139) lists send, slash, wait_turn, sleep, exit_clean as genuinely implemented (verified by reading the dispatch case block directly: send|slash → step_send, wait_turn → step_wait_turn, sleep → sleep N, exit_clean → step_exit_clean; every other step type is an explicit not_implemented stub). This scenario's recipe needs only send + wait_turn + sleep — all present. The three critical defects the #1960 driver audit found (untrusted-workspace modal swallowing the first message; no inter-keystroke delay dropping Enter; resolve_transcript landing on a subagent's shadow transcript) were fixed in commit 0239a1bd ("fix(muse): repair the recording driver so it can't record a corrupted pass"), which is the current HEAD of this branch.

## Vacuous-pass condition (load-bearing environment property)

Under what condition would this cell pass while proving nothing? If the recipe's prompt happened to route through the kind:"approval" review flow instead of the policy fast-track — even though this machine's :auto-review profile resolves that flow automatically via an LLM judge (decision_source.kind:"llm_judge", format-spec §5) rather than blocking on a human — the daemon would still open/close a transcript-tier PermissionPending window (PermissionRequestIDs/PermissionResolvedIDs), which the state_classifier could read as a transient `waiting`. That would make this recording indistinguishable from the *different* scenario (a permission-gated tool call), not the auto-executed one this cell claims to test — and a human reviewer would not detect the substitution just from a green 3/3, exactly the copilot 2-11 shape this rule exists to catch. The recipe therefore deliberately mirrors the ONE command shape format-spec §4 actually observed getting `policy_decision:"allow:policy"` (`bash "ls -la"`) rather than an unverified analogy — no sample in the corpus confirms how a differently-worded command (e.g. `echo hello`) classifies. This machine's specific :auto-review permission-profile behavior for read-only listing commands is therefore a load-bearing precondition of this recipe, named in `caveats` and `recipe.preconditions` below.
caveats: Not yet recorded end-to-end for muse — no prior recording exists for this cell (0 cells recorded for muse across the whole matrix at assessment time). This verdict is grounded in the built adapter's code + tests + the muse-format-spec.md live corpus, not a live run of THIS scenario; record is what promotes it from provisional to settled.

Load-bearing environment property (vacuous-pass rule): this machine's muse install runs a ':auto-review' permission profile that fast-tracks certain read-only bash commands via policy_decision:'allow:policy' (no approval flow, no wait) while routing others through an automated kind:'approval' review (auto-resolved by an LLM judge, but still opens a transcript-tier permission-pending window). The recipe deliberately uses the ONE command shape (`ls -la`) directly evidenced as policy-fast-tracked in muse-format-spec.md §4. If a different muse version, account, or permission-profile configuration routes plain read-only listing commands through review instead, this recipe would silently start exercising the OTHER scenario (permission-gated tool call) and the cell needs re-verification at record time.

terminal:'cancelled' semantics are UNVERIFIED (muse-format-spec.md §3/§12: no sample confirms whether it represents a genuine human ESC or purely programmatic cancellation) — not load-bearing for this scenario since the happy path asserts terminal:'completed', but noted for completeness.

A nonzero tool exit_code's on-disk shape has never been captured live (muse-format-spec.md, task context) — irrelevant here since this scenario's tool call is expected to succeed, but the parser's IsError-from-exit_code path (parser_test.go:298, marked SYNTHETIC in that test's own comment) is unverified against a live failing call.

The muse-format-spec.md corpus was gathered partly while ANOTHER live recording session (for different scenarios: 2-14/4-1/5-1) was concurrently running on this machine — noted by that doc's own author as a concurrency caveat; it does not affect the specific event shapes cited here (turn boundaries, tool-call pairing, approval family), which were also cross-checked directly against the parser's own doc comments written while reading the second time.

LIVE-CONFIRMED (record pass, #1960, recording 2026-09-14-04-47-31, session 01a09dd0-0803-7961-bdd0-3fb88305d5ef): this machine's :auto-review profile STILL classifies 'ls -la' as policy_decision:'allow:policy' (single occurrence in the raw transcript, zero kind:'approval' records) -- the load-bearing precondition held. BUT the recording exposed a genuine vacuous-pass bug in the ORIGINAL expected.jsonl: turn_start/turn_end were left unpinned (no same_session_as), and muse's goal-reminder/verify-reminder subagents (spawned for every prompt, format-spec §9) go straight to working (skipping ready) before the parent session's own turn starts. One subagent's own read-only arc (working at +9.5s after birth, back to ready 4.9s later, no waiting in between) fully satisfied the unpinned ready->working->ready-with-no-waiting shape on its own, so the original spec PASSED 3/3 while validating a SUBAGENT's reminder turn instead of the parent session's actual ls -la tool call -- confirmed via expected-validate's phase report (turn_start/turn_end both matched session 35c6c413-5c09-4c10-9b66-daee87a1d0d1, not the parent). This is the identical vacuous-pass mechanism independently found and fixed in the sibling turn-end-terminal-text cell during the same record pass. Fixed by pinning turn_start and turn_end to same_session_as:session_birth. Also corrected cost_nonzero from true to false: muse-spark-1.3-contributor has no litellm pricing/alias entry (confirmed live -- daemon logs 'no pricing for model ... cost will be 0' on every recording of this onboarding pass); the original value was copied from the claudecode sibling template without re-deriving it for muse's own unpriced model, matching the same defect already documented for the basic-turn and turn-end-terminal-text sibling cells.

preconditions: muse CLI on PATH and authenticated (muse login or META_API_KEY) — confirmed installed at 1.2.1 on this machine

This machine's muse permission profile classifies a plain 'ls -la' read-only bash command as policy_decision:'allow:policy' (no approval flow) — re-probe this at record time; if the live run instead shows a kind:'approval' record for this call, the recipe is exercising the WRONG scenario and needs a different command or a policy-profile check first

script.text: List the files in the current directory using ls -la, then reply 'done'.

verify: events.jsonl shows the session entering ready, then exactly one ready→working transition and one working→ready transition
events.jsonl contains at least one tool-call open/close pair (bash) inside the working span
events.jsonl contains NO state_transition to waiting for this session during the entire run
transcript shows the literal final reply token 'done'
